newsitem.title: UK: Atlantic Telecom unit wins Scottish licence.
newsitem.headline: Atlantic Telecom unit wins Scottish licence.

text.p: Britain's Atlantic Telecom Group said on Monday its wholly owned subsidiary Atlantic Telecommunications Ltd has received a licence to operate services in the east of Scotland.
The area comprises the former regions of Grampian, Tayside, Central, Fife and Lothian, including the main cities of Aberdeen, Dundee and Edinburgh.

"This licence gives us the ability to develop our service outside the Glasgow/Strathclyde area, where we have our current licence, to the rest of the more populated areas of Scotland," chairman Graham J Duncan said.
He added the licence would double the estimated area which the company could serve.
